subject: Success signal ladder + evaluation runbook for HealthSync pilot
messages:
From: Ellen Park <ellen@healthsync.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aaron Cho <aaron.cho@healthsync.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Success signal ladder + evaluation runbook for HealthSync pilot

Hi Priyom / Laura,

Thanks for taking this on. We want to formalize the evaluation for the HealthSync ingestion pilot so that our internal stakeholders can sign off quickly. High level asks:

- A "success signal ladder" that defines progressive checkpoints (smoke -> functional -> quantitative)
- Concrete acceptance tests for each checkpoint (pass/fail criteria, sampling size)
- Clear exit gates (what causes a pause/rollback vs go/no-go)
- A short runbook for the smoke tests we can run during the first two pilot weeks

Attached: initial data schema and a short list of top-priority flows.

We aim to start the pilot the week of Apr 19 and have a decision meeting on May 3. Can you share a mutual action plan (MAP) and an evaluation runbook by EOD Apr 4?

Thanks,
Ellen
Ellen Park
Head of Data Ops, HealthSync
ellen@healthsync.com

Attachments: healthsync-data-schema.json (attached)
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Park <ellen@healthsync.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Success signal ladder + evaluation runbook for HealthSync pilot

Thanks Ellen — we can do that. Draft below is the proposed structure; I attached a workbook (pilot-signal-ladder.xlsx) and a short smoke-test markdown with concrete steps.

Summary (what we'll deliver by EOD Apr 4):
- Success signal ladder (3 tiers): Smoke, Functional, Baseline KPI
- Acceptance test suite: 12 targeted checks + sampling plan
- Exit gate definitions and who owns the decision
- MAP with timeline to production decision (includes dates you suggested)
- Smoke runbook (timeboxed 30–60 min checks)

Quick highlights from the ladder:
- Smoke: end-to-end inference path with 10 representative records; must return valid structured output and no runtime errors.
- Functional: 100 sample records across high-volume flows; accuracy heuristics (field-level concordance >= 90% for key fields).
- Baseline KPI: latency P95 < 450ms, throughput >= 50 req/s sustained for 30m, token-level cost delta within agreed band.

Exit gates (examples):
- Pause pilot if smoke fails on >2/10 records or any security violation is detected.
- Rollback to previous model variant if functional accuracy < 80% on 100-sample test.

I've put owners in the workbook and a proposed sign-off matrix. Please review and tell us if these thresholds are too strict; we can tune before the pilot start.

Priyom
Priyom Das
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.ai

Attachments: pilot-signal-ladder.xlsx, smoke-test-cases.md

Date: Sat, 03 Apr 2027 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Success signal ladder + evaluation runbook for HealthSync pilot

Thanks — nice initial draft. Two suggested edits before we finalize:

1) Add an automated nightly smoke run that checks the top 3 flows against a small golden set (5 items each) and reports results to the MAP dashboard. This should catch regressions outside the manual window.

2) Make the acceptance test sampling explicit: for functional tests we recommend stratified sampling across shopper, claim, and provider flows: 40/30/30 split to ensure coverage of edge cases.

Also, for the MAP timeline:
- Apr 19: Pilot kickoff (data ingest enabled, minimal pre-production traffic)
- Apr 26: End of smoke week; we run full functional suite and produce a short report
- May 3: Go/no-go review with execs (we'll present the success ladder and sample artifacts)

I've flagged a potential blocker: HealthSync's ingestion schema has optional fields that affect concordance checks — I'll add a note in the workbook with a per-field tolerance.

Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Solutions & Onramp, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai
From: Ellen Park <ellen@healthsync.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 03 Apr 2027 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Success signal ladder + evaluation runbook for HealthSync pilot

This looks good — thank you. A couple of follow-ups from our side:

- Can you add a short canary checklist that specifies how many live requests we send during kickoff (we prefer <5% of traffic) and the target window for monitoring?
- We need the manual and automated smoke results exported to a place our security team can access for audit (S3 link or shared Drive).
- For rollback conditions: please add a short rollback play that includes a quick revert path to the previous model and who executes the revert. We also need the security contact included in the MAP for immediate escalation.

If you can add those by EOD Apr 4, we should be able to review and confirm the go/no-go timeline.

Thanks,
Ellen
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Park <ellen@healthsync.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 04 Apr 2027 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Success signal ladder + evaluation runbook for HealthSync pilot

Ellen — attaching the consolidated MAP + runbook (mutual-action-plan-v1.pdf). Highlights from the final runbook:

- Canary checklist: < 5% sampled traffic for 2 hours; monitor error rate + schema concordance in 5-min buckets. Canaries auto-fail if error rate > 1% or concordance drops > 10 points vs baseline.
- Automated nightly smoke: runs at 02:00 UTC, checks 3 flows, reports to the MAP dashboard (Drive link included).
- Acceptance tests (short):
  * Smoke — 10 records, pass = no runtime error AND structured payload present
  * Functional — 100 stratified records (40/30/30), pass = field-level concordance >= 90% for key fields; sample exceptions documented
  * Baseline KPI — latency P95 < 450ms, throughput >= 50 req/s sustained 30m
- Exit/rollback: immediate pause if smoke fails >2/10 OR any security violation; rollback path = model pin to previous variant (handled by infra ops) with runbook steps (failover, scoreboard, and postmortem owner).

Next steps:
- Ellen: confirm if the thresholds above are acceptable and whether security should be cc'd on the May 3 review.
- HealthSync: sign MAP PDF or provide redlines by Apr 7 so we can lock the pilot plan.

I've included the Drive folder with logs and the smoke test output in the PDF's links.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
